Verdict: the intent is sound, but the Codex PR gate is not currently reliable or enforced.

Key findings:

- The gate can falsely associate a `+1` with the wrong commit. [AGENTS.md](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/petspotr/AGENTS.md:130) records the cutoff before pushing, but a review of the previous head could finish after that cutoff. Reactions do not contain a reviewed SHA.
- OpenAI officially documents `@codex review`, the 👀 progress reaction, automatic review on PR opening, and review bodies containing findings. It does not promise reruns after every push or document `+1` as a stable API contract. The repository currently exhibits both behaviors, but they are integration-specific. [Official Codex GitHub documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/third-party/github)
- The live GitHub ruleset does not enforce this gate: approving reviews are `0`, thread resolution is disabled, and no Codex status check is required. Consequently, [PR #100](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/pull/100) merged five minutes before Codex posted findings against its final head. [PR #95](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/pull/95) similarly merged before four Codex findings arrived.
- The file lacks the officially recommended `## Code Review Rules` section. Add two or three durable PetSpotR-specific rules covering Pub/Sub idempotency, backward-compatible event schemas, and exposure or mutation of user data. Mechanical checks should remain in CI.
- The local pre-commit `code-review` subagent and the GitHub Codex reviewer are different gates. That distinction should be explicit.

I recommend rewriting step 11 around this sequence:

1. Push and wait until GitHub reports the expected full head SHA.
2. Post `@codex review` for that head and record the trigger comment timestamp.
3. Treat 👀 only as progress.
4. Accept `+1` only when created after that trigger and while the head remains unchanged.
5. Validate any review body’s `Reviewed commit` against the expected SHA.
6. Address and resolve every actionable Codex thread, then repeat from step 1 after any new commit.
7. Merge only after the final exact head receives a clean result.

For actual enforcement, add a required “Codex review gate” status check; enabling required thread resolution would also help but would not prevent merging before Codex responds.

The broader document also needs cleanup:

- [AGENTS.md](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/petspotr/AGENTS.md:16) says there is no frontend, while line 181 correctly says UI review is live.
- It describes four services, but `web-frontend` makes five.

- `docker-compose` is not installed here; `docker compose` is. Compose now pulls the Ollama model itself.

No files were changed during this audit.
